title: Dynamic Routes
definition: Routes that are not fixed strings, but act as variables to capture data from the URL (like an ID or a slug). Created by wrapping a folder name in square brackets: `[param]`.
simpleExplanation: If you have 10,000 blog posts, you can't create 10,000 folders. You create ONE folder called `[slug]`. If the user visits `/blog/my-trip-to-japan`, Next.js routes it to the `[slug]` folder and passes 'my-trip-to-japan' into your component as a variable.
realWorldExample: An e-commerce site where `/products/123` and `/products/456` both use the exact same React component, but fetch different product data based on the ID.

basic: How do you define a dynamic route folder that captures a user's ID?
intermediate: How do you access the dynamic variable inside your `page.tsx` component?

answers.question: How to define?
answers.answer: Name the folder with square brackets: `[id]` or `[userId]`.

answers.question: How to access?
answers.answer: Next.js automatically passes a `params` prop to your page component. You would access it via `params.id`.
